patterns: APPSC asks the bare identification: Tenth Schedule = anti-defection = 52nd Amendment 1985 (APPSC-GS 2019).
Other PSCs repeat: first constitutional recognition of parties (1985), J&K's own law (1979), merger needs two-thirds.
Exception questions: presiding officer giving up and rejoining party; merger vs deleted one-third split.
UPSC 2025 adds who decides (Speaker, no EC opinion) - app covers this well.
App MCQs go far beyond PYQ depth with case law (Subhash Desai, Keisham), privileges procedure and 2026 merger disputes.
